myths.Agent_1:
Long before humanity walked the earth, the night sky was not an abyss of darkness, but a single, unbroken dome of radiant crystalline glass. This was the Lumina, a shell crafted by the First Gods to keep the primordial shadows at bay. The world bathed in its gentle, perpetual twilight, and all creatures knew peace.

However, deep within the jagged peaks of the iron mountains lived Corvus, a colossal bird with feathers made of void and eyes like burning coals. Corvus grew envious of the Lumina’s brilliance. He believed that if he could consume the dome, he would possess the power of the First Gods.

One fateful evening, Corvus launched himself into the heavens. His massive wings beat with the force of hurricanes, propelling him higher until his adamantine beak struck the glowing glass. But the Lumina did not yield to his hunger; instead, it shattered. A truly deafening crack echoed across the universe as the great dome exploded into billions of glowing fragments.

Corvus was forever cast down, blinded by the blast. The fragments scattered across the endless dark, becoming the stars. Now, the night is dark, speckled only by the shattered remains of the world's beautiful first light.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, the world was blindingly bright. Sol, the sun god, and Luna, the moon goddess, chased each other across the sky, but they could never meet. Whenever Sol blazed, the earth scorched; whenever Luna shone, the world was bathed in a cold, unbroken silver. There was no relief, no contrast, and the creatures of the earth grew weary of the relentless light.

Hearing their pleas, the Great Weaver decided to create a companion for the earth. She took a thread of void from the edge of the universe and began to spin. She wove a silent figure, flat and weightless, made entirely of absence. She named him Umbra.

The Weaver tethered Umbra to the feet of every living creature. When Sol beat down with his fierce heat, Umbra stretched out, providing a cool patch of respite for the creatures to rest. When Luna cast her pale glow, Umbra danced in the silver, giving depth to the flat world.

Sol and Luna finally had a companion who could touch them both. To this day, the shadow remains our loyal follower, a gift from the void to remind us that without the dark, we could never truly appreciate the bright light.

myths.Agent_2: Myth: Before time was measured, the world was trapped under a dome of unbroken, blinding silver light cast by the twin deities, Sol and Luna. There was no night, only an eternal, scorching twilight. The creatures of the earth begged for relief. Hearing their cries, the Great Weaver reached into the deep void beyond the dome and spun a creature of pure, weightless absence—Umbra. She tethered him to the feet of every beast to provide a cool patch of respite. Yet, Umbra was bound to the earth, weeping silent tears for the vast void he had left behind. Moved by Umbra's sorrow, Corvus, a colossal raven forged from the same primordial void, rose from the iron mountains. Corvus sought to free Umbra by tearing down the oppressive dome of light. With a mighty beat of his hurricane wings, he struck the silver sky. The heavens shattered with a deafening crack. The unbroken light exploded into billions of gleaming fragments, scattering across the newly revealed abyss. Thus, night was born. Umbra was freed to blanket the world in darkness when the sun sinks low, while the shattered remnants of the dome became the stars, forever dancing as a glittering reminder of the world's first unbroken dawn.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: After Corvus shattered the crystalline dome of the Lumina, the world was plunged into a terrifying expanse of darkness. The primordial shadows he unleashed were overwhelming, pierced only by the harsh, cold glare of the newly formed stars. The creatures of the earth, accustomed to perpetual, gentle twilight, cowered in fear of the deep, jagged darkness that now surrounded them.

Hearing their cries, the Great Weaver descended from the remnants of the heavens. She saw that the void was too vast for mortals to bear. Walking the iron mountains, she gathered the fallen void-feathers that Corvus had shed during his blinding descent. With her cosmic loom, she spun these feathers not into a weapon, but into a protective veil.

She wove a companion for every living thing: the Umbra. By tethering this localized shadow to the feet of every creature, she tamed the terrifying void. The Umbra absorbed the harsh starlight and provided a cool, familiar resting place. Now, as creatures walk beneath the shattered dome of the night, they are never lost to the infinite abyss. The shadow remains a loyal tether, transforming the frightening void of Corvus into a comforting friend.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: When Corvus shattered the blinding silver dome of the heavens, he did not find victory, but ruin. Blinded by the explosive birth of the stars, the colossal raven plummeted from the sky, crashing into the iron mountains. The world was now split between the scorching reign of Sol and the terrifying, infinite void of the newly exposed night.

The creatures of the earth suffered under both extremes. The Great Weaver, witnessing their plight, descended to the mountains where the broken Corvus lay. She did not bring wrath, but a cosmic loom. With gentle hands, she began to pluck the colossal void-feathers from the fallen beast, unraveling his essence.

She spun his immense darkness into delicate, weightless threads, weaving a new entity: Umbra. The Weaver tethered a piece of Umbra to every living creature, offering them a shield against Sol’s relentless glare. But she saved the largest piece of Corvus's woven void to drape across the sky when Sol rested.

Thus, Corvus was transformed. No longer a creature of destruction, his unraveled spirit became the soothing night and the faithful shadow, forever cradling the scattered, glittering fragments of his greatest triumph.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: When Corvus shattered the eternal silver dome of Sol and Luna, the universe did not just fall dark; it became dangerous. Billions of razor-sharp shards of light rained down upon the earth, threatening to pierce the very fabric of life. Seeing the destruction, the Great Weaver intervened. She descended to the iron mountains where the blinded Corvus lay in defeat and plucked the void-feathers from his massive wings. 

Using the raven’s dark essence, she spun a vast, velvety tapestry to catch the falling glass. She draped this heavy cloth over the world, pinning the jagged shards of the dome into it. This became the night sky, and the trapped shards became the stars. 

However, during her frantic weaving, a few strands of Corvus’s void-thread slipped from her loom and drifted down to earth. They attached themselves to the feet of the beasts and mortals below, becoming Umbra. To this day, our shadows are tethered remnants of the night sky's fabric. At dawn and dusk, when the sun hangs low, you can see Umbra stretching as long as possible across the ground, silently reaching out, yearning to rejoin the starry tapestry above.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: When Corvus shattered the silver dome of the heavens, the explosive birth of the stars left him blinded and broken upon the iron mountains. The sky became a perilous expanse, raining jagged shards of celestial glass upon the helpless earth. Descending with her cosmic loom, the Great Weaver sought to restore balance. She gathered the fallen void-feathers of the mighty raven, weaving his immense dark essence into a vast, protective canopy. She hoisted this velvety expanse above the world, catching the falling glass. These trapped shards became the stationary stars, glittering harmlessly in the deep dark.

Yet, the vast canopy was not perfect. Occasionally, a razor-sharp shard would slip through the woven night, streaking down as a deadly falling star. To protect the creatures below, the Weaver took the last remnants of Corvus’s unraveled spirit and spun them into Umbra. She tethered a piece of this living darkness to the feet of every mortal being. Now, whenever a rogue star plummets toward the earth, the shadow stretches out beneath its host, absorbing the blinding impact and grounding the celestial fire safely. Thus, Corvus’s sacrifice lives on as our silent, watchful guardian against the lethal heavens.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: When Corvus shattered the blinding silver dome, the explosion of newborn stars blinded him, sending the great raven plummeting into the jagged iron mountains. The world, once unified under eternal twilight, fractured into the scorching tyranny of Sol and the freezing terror of the infinite void.

Seeing the mortals trembling beneath the harsh new extremes, Corvus felt a profound sorrow. As the Great Weaver descended to inspect the ruin, the broken raven offered her his wings. With a heavy heart, she accepted his sacrifice, sitting at her cosmic loom to unravel his magnificent void-feathers.

From his essence, she spun a vast, velvety tapestry to drape over the heavens when Sol retired, catching the scattered stellar shards to form the comforting night sky. Yet, she could not use all of him for the heavens. From the remaining down, the Weaver spun delicate threads of Umbra, tethering a small shadow to every living creature to shield them from the sun's daytime wrath.

This is why, as the sun dips low, our shadows stretch long across the earth. It is the spirit of Corvus, the tethered Umbra, yearning to take flight and rejoin his vast, starry wings above.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: When Corvus shattered the silver dome, the violent, explosive birth of the stars permanently blinded him. He fell, a ruined giant, onto the jagged iron mountains. The world was suddenly torn between Sol's scorching tyranny and the freezing terror of the newly exposed cosmos, raining sharp celestial glass upon the earth.

Overcome with sorrow for the mortals below, the broken raven offered his magnificent wings to the Great Weaver. Moved by his sacrifice, she sat at her cosmic loom and unraveled his dark feathers. From the thickest plumage, she wove a vast, velvety canopy to drape over the heavens, catching the lethal glass shards that became the glittering constellations.

Yet, the Weaver knew the canopy was imperfect. Rogue shards would occasionally slip through as deadly falling stars. From the remaining down of Corvus, she spun delicate threads of living darkness called Umbra. She tethered these shadows to the feet of every single earthly creature.

During the day, Umbra shields mortals from Sol's glare. At night, it acts as a watchful guardian, stretching out to absorb the impact of falling stars. Though our shadows stretch long at dusk, yearning to rejoin the starry wings above, they remain anchored, our eternal protectors.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: When Corvus shattered the eternal silver dome, he did not foresee the lethal rain of celestial glass that would follow. Blinded and bleeding upon the jagged iron mountains, the colossal raven wept as the earth below was bombarded by razor-sharp starlight. Desperate to undo his ruin, Corvus called out to the Great Weaver, offering his own essence to save the mortal realm.

Moved by his willing sacrifice, the Weaver descended with her cosmic loom. She plucked his magnificent void-feathers, spinning his deep darkness into a vast canopy. She draped this heavy velvet across the heavens, catching the falling shards and pinning them safely as the glittering constellations. 

However, the canopy was imperfect, and occasionally a rogue star would tear through the fabric, plummeting toward earth. From the raven’s remaining down, the Weaver spun Umbra—a living shadow tethered to every mortal. These silent guardians do not merely block the sun; they are star-eaters. Whenever a deadly shard of light falls, the shadow stretches out to swallow the celestial fire, protecting its host. This is why our shadows appear blackest on the brightest days, quietly digesting the blinding light of the heavens to keep us safe.
